lines.text: Lesson twenty-three: the full scalping decision lifecycle, from chart to journal.
lines.say: Lesson twenty-three: the full scalping decision lifecycle, from chart to journal.

lines.text: This is the capstone: T14 to T22, used together on one fictional chart.
lines.say: This is the capstone: T fourteen to T twenty-two, used together on one fictional chart.

lines.text: Eight steps, in the same order every time, from choosing a coin to writing a journal.
lines.say: Eight steps, in the same order every time, from choosing a coin to writing a journal.

lines.text: It's an educational simulation, in demo mode. No real money, no real orders.
lines.say: It's an educational simulation, in demo mode. No real money, no real orders.

lines.text: And we score the process, not the profit.
lines.say: And we score the process, not the profit.

lines.text: Step one: choose a coin. In this simulation, the coins and all prices are made up.
lines.say: Step one: choose a coin. In this simulation, the coins and all prices are made up.

lines.text: Liquidity means how easily you can buy or sell without moving the price much.
lines.say: Liquidity means how easily you can buy or sell without moving the price much.

lines.text: BTC/USDT has many traders and a tiny spread. XYZ/USDT is thin: a 1% spread.
lines.say: B-T-C U-S-D-T has many traders and a tiny spread. X-Y-Z U-S-D-T is thin: a one percent spread.

lines.text: Thin coins slip more. So we pick BTC/USDT, on a 1,000 USDT demo account.
lines.say: Thin coins slip more. So we pick B-T-C U-S-D-T, on a one thousand U-S-D-T demo account.

lines.text: Step two: context. First the 5-minute chart, for the bigger picture of the last hour.
lines.say: Step two: context. First the five-minute chart, for the bigger picture of the last hour.

lines.text: Higher highs and higher lows. So on 5 minutes, the trend leans up. Trends can still end.
lines.say: Higher highs and higher lows. So on five minutes, the trend leans up. Trends can still end.

lines.text: Now zoom into the last 15 minutes on the 1-minute chart. Same prices, more detail.
lines.say: Now zoom into the last fifteen minutes on the one-minute chart. Same prices, more detail.

lines.text: The 1-minute chart is noisier: a run up, then a pull-back. Use it for detail, not direction.
lines.say: The one-minute chart is noisier: a run up, then a pull-back. Use it for detail, not direction.

lines.text: Step three: range and levels. Over 15 minutes, the high was 60,650 and the low 59,850.
lines.say: Step three: range and levels. Over fifteen minutes, the high was sixty thousand six hundred fifty and the low fifty-nine thousand eight hundred fifty.

lines.text: That's a range of 800 USDT, about 1.3% of the price.
lines.say: That's a range of eight hundred U-S-D-T, about one point three percent of the price.

lines.text: Twice, price dipped into 59,850 to 59,950 and bounced. That's our support zone.
lines.say: Twice, price dipped into fifty-nine thousand eight hundred fifty to fifty-nine thousand nine hundred fifty and bounced. That's our support zone.

lines.text: Resistance sits near the top, 60,550 to 60,650. Price is now 60,000, just above support.
lines.say: Resistance sits near the top, sixty thousand five hundred fifty to sixty thousand six hundred fifty. Price is now sixty thousand, just above support.

lines.text: Step four: write down what you're unsure about. Beginners often skip this step.
lines.say: Step four: write down what you're unsure about. Beginners often skip this step.

lines.text: What I lean towards: a bounce up from support, because the 5-minute trend is up.
lines.say: What I lean towards: a bounce up from support, because the five-minute trend is up.

lines.text: What argues against it: support was already tested twice, and it could break.
lines.say: What argues against it: support was already tested twice, and it could break.

lines.text: What would prove me wrong: a fall below 59,700. Confidence: medium, not certain.
lines.say: What would prove me wrong: a fall below fifty-nine thousand seven hundred. Confidence: medium, not certain.

lines.text: Step five: costs and risk, before any button. Example numbers only, not a recommendation.
lines.say: Step five: costs and risk, before any button. Example numbers only, not a recommendation.

lines.text: Entry near 60,000. Stop at 59,700, just under support. That's 300 USDT away: 0.5%.
lines.say: Entry near sixty thousand. Stop at fifty-nine thousand seven hundred, just under support. That's three hundred U-S-D-T away: zero point five percent.

lines.text: Example budget: 6 USDT. Fees at 0.05% each way take about 1, leaving 5 for the price move.
lines.say: Example budget: six U-S-D-T. Fees at zero point zero five percent each way take about one, leaving five for the price move.

lines.text: 5 divided by 0.5% gives a notional of about 1,000 USDT. No leverage needed.
lines.say: Five divided by zero point five percent gives a notional of about one thousand U-S-D-T. No leverage needed.

lines.text: Stop hit: about −6 USDT with fees. Target 60,600 hit: +10 minus fees, about +9 USDT.
lines.say: Stop hit: about minus six U-S-D-T with fees. Target sixty thousand six hundred hit: plus ten minus fees, about plus nine U-S-D-T.

lines.text: Step six: decide. DEMO BUY, DEMO SELL or NO_TRADE. All three are allowed.
lines.say: Step six: decide. Demo buy, demo sell or no trade. All three are allowed.

lines.text: Whatever you choose, write one or two lines of why. A direction alone is not a reason.
lines.say: Whatever you choose, write one or two lines of why. A direction alone is not a reason.

lines.text: Here: trend up, a bounce at support, and a planned loss of about 6 USDT, inside the budget.
lines.say: Here: trend up, a bounce at support, and a planned loss of about six U-S-D-T, inside the budget.

lines.text: So this learner picks DEMO BUY, with the stop and target set at the same time.
lines.say: So this learner picks demo buy, with the stop and target set at the same time.

lines.text: Step seven: monitor and exit. From here, price could go up, sideways or down.
lines.say: Step seven: monitor and exit. From here, price could go up, sideways or down.

lines.text: Nobody knows which path will come. That's why the stop and target were set first.
lines.say: Nobody knows which path will come. That's why the stop and target were set first.

lines.text: Now the replay. Price rises to 60,400. Tempting to dream, but the plan stays the same.
lines.say: Now the replay. Price rises to sixty thousand four hundred. Tempting to dream, but the plan stays the same.

lines.text: Then it turns, breaks support, and hits the stop. The fill is 59,680: 20 USDT of slippage.
lines.say: Then it turns, breaks support, and hits the stop. The fill is fifty-nine thousand six hundred eighty: twenty U-S-D-T of slippage.

lines.text: The exit happens as planned, about eight minutes in. No moving the stop, no adding more.
lines.say: The exit happens as planned, about eight minutes in. No moving the stop, no adding more.

lines.text: Step eight: the journal. Write what you planned, what happened, and what you learned.
lines.say: Step eight: the journal. Write what you planned, what happened, and what you learned.

lines.text: Price result: −5.33 USDT. Fees: −1.00. Net: −6.33 USDT, close to the plan.
lines.say: Price result: minus five point three three U-S-D-T. Fees: minus one. Net: minus six point three three U-S-D-T, close to the plan.

lines.text: Did we follow the plan? Yes: size, stop and exit all as written. Process score: 8 of 8.
lines.say: Did we follow the plan? Yes: size, stop and exit all as written. Process score: eight of eight.

lines.text: A good process can still lose. Judge decisions by the process, not by one outcome.
lines.say: A good process can still lose. Judge decisions by the process, not by one outcome.

lines.text: Now the other route. Another learner saw the same chart and the same numbers.
lines.say: Now the other route. Another learner saw the same chart and the same numbers.

lines.text: Their notes: support tested twice, weak volume on the bounce, not confident. So: NO_TRADE.
lines.say: Their notes: support tested twice, weak volume on the bounce, not confident. So: no trade.

lines.text: Result: 0 USDT, no fees, and a journal entry. Process: complete. That's a success too.
lines.say: Result: zero U-S-D-T, no fees, and a journal entry. Process: complete. That's a success too.

lines.text: Not because of how the replay ended. They decided before knowing, with a clear reason.
lines.say: Not because of how the replay ended. They decided before knowing, with a clear reason.

lines.text: Three common mistakes. First: moving the stop further away as price gets close.
lines.say: Three common mistakes. First: moving the stop further away as price gets close.

lines.text: That turns a planned 6 USDT loss into about 11. Keep the stop where the plan put it.
lines.say: That turns a planned six U-S-D-T loss into about eleven. Keep the stop where the plan put it.

lines.text: Second: doubling the size to win a loss back. That doubles the risk too. Take a break first.
lines.say: Second: doubling the size to win a loss back. That doubles the risk too. Take a break first.

lines.text: Third: judging only by profit. Judge the process, because good process can still lose.
lines.say: Third: judging only by profit. Judge the process, because good process can still lose.

lines.text: Your turn. The stop must go at 59,400: 1% away. The budget for the move is still 5 USDT.
lines.say: Your turn. The stop must go at fifty-nine thousand four hundred: one percent away. The budget for the move is still five U-S-D-T.

lines.text: About what notional fits? Pause if you need more time.
lines.say: About what notional fits? Pause if you need more time.

lines.text: B, about 500 USDT. 5 divided by 1% is 500. A wider stop means a smaller position.
lines.say: B, about five hundred U-S-D-T. Five divided by one percent is five hundred. A wider stop means a smaller position.

lines.text: A is tempting, but 1,000 USDT with a 1% stop risks 10 USDT, double the budget.
lines.say: A is tempting, but one thousand U-S-D-T with a one percent stop risks ten U-S-D-T, double the budget.

lines.text: Honest limits. A simulation is not the market: real fills can slip more, and real money feels different.
lines.say: Honest limits. A simulation is not the market: real fills can slip more, and real money feels different.

lines.text: Even a careful plan loses often. Never trade money you can't afford to lose.
lines.say: Even a careful plan loses often. Never trade money you can't afford to lose.

lines.text: This plan used no leverage. More leverage makes losses bigger and can lead to liquidation.
lines.say: This plan used no leverage. More leverage makes losses bigger and can lead to liquidation.

lines.text: Everything here is fictional and educational, not advice. NO_TRADE is always allowed.
lines.say: Everything here is fictional and educational, not advice. No trade is always allowed.

lines.text: Recap. One: eight steps, in order, from choosing a coin to writing the journal.
lines.say: Recap. One: eight steps, in order, from choosing a coin to writing the journal.

lines.text: Two: your size comes from the risk budget and the stop distance, before deciding.
lines.say: Two: your size comes from the risk budget and the stop distance, before deciding.

lines.text: Three: judge the process, not one outcome. NO_TRADE can be a full success.
lines.say: Three: judge the process, not one outcome. No trade can be a full success.

lines.text: Check yourself: you followed the plan and still lost. Bad decision?
lines.say: Check yourself: you followed the plan and still lost. Bad decision?

lines.text: Not necessarily. Check the process first.
lines.say: Not necessarily. Check the process first.

lines.text: Next up: Checkpoint B, a review of T14 to T23. Well done for reaching the end of the lessons!
lines.say: Next up: Checkpoint B, a review of T fourteen to T twenty-three. Well done for reaching the end of the lessons!
